cards.title: A leading VAR=value on an Allrun command is the environment of that one step
cards.when: parsing or porting an Allrun that writes `USE_ARC=true runApplication -s arc extrudeMesh`
cards.statement: RunFunctions forwards a variable written before the command through the environment, so such a line is a command with an env prefix, not a variable assignment. A parser whose assignment branch matches `^\w+=.*$` swallows the whole line and the step silently disappears from the plan.
recipe: treat `VAR=value ` before a command as the env of that step and keep it in the log line
treat a bare `VAR=value` (no trailing command) as a shell variable and expand it later
assert on the parsed step count: polyline Allrun has 8 steps, the buggy parser produced 4
evidence: exp-025 tut-16 before the fix: 4 steps, then `FOAM FATAL ERROR: Cannot find file "points" in directory "polyMesh" in times "1"`
exp-025 tut-16 after the fix: 8 steps, 51 400 cells, maxNonOrtho 32.4679, PASS

cards.title: np must match decomposeParDict only when the plan actually calls mpirun
cards.when: running a tutorial case that ships a system/decomposeParDict but never starts runParallel
cards.statement: Refusing any np mismatch is too strict: several serial tutorials carry a decomposeParDict with many subdomains. The check must be limited to plans that contain a parallel step; a serial plan simply ignores np. When a parallel step does exist, rewriting numberOfSubdomains breaks hierarchical decomposition.
recipe: compute needsParallel = steps.some(step => step.parallel)
refuse a mismatch only when needsParallel is true, and suggest np = numberOfSubdomains
never rewrite only numberOfSubdomains of a hierarchical decomposition
evidence: exp-025 tut-15: np=1 accepted after the fix, 8 steps, 13 cells, 28.3936° (gate FAIL on face weights)
snappyHexMesh/insidePoints/system/decomposeParDict = 6 and the Allrun does run in parallel — there the refusal stands

cards.title: moveDynamicMesh is a solver: mesh-only stops before it and leaves the raw blockMesh
cards.when: running blockMesh/pipe or any moveDynamicMesh tutorial with steps: "mesh-only"
cards.statement: moveDynamicMesh is a motion solver and also compiles a dynamicCode library, so in mesh-only mode it is skipped. What remains is the raw blockMesh result — for blockMesh/pipe maxNonOrtho 80.7713 — and the quality gate rightly fails. This is expected, not a defect: with steps: "all" the smoothing runs.
recipe: for a motion tutorial use steps: "all" (and a timeout), or accept a documented gate FAIL in mesh-only
do not tune the gate profile to make the raw mesh pass
record the skipped step in the manifest `skipped[]` with its reason
evidence: exp-025 tut-09_blockMesh_pipe and tut-11_blockMesh_pipe: 2 816 cells, maxNonOrtho 80.7713, gate FAIL
moveDynamicMesh in mesh-only before the skip: `Could not load …/dynamicCode/…/librelaxationFactor_<hash>.so` then SIGSEGV

cards.title: checkMesh -writeFields writes into 0/, so an overlay must copy 0/ instead of linking it
cards.when: running the quality gate with writeFields to obtain a per-cell quality field
cards.statement: The gate runs checkMesh inside a disposable overlay with system/ copied and polyMesh/ linked. `-writeFields '(nonOrthoAngle)'` writes the field into `<overlay>/0/`, so if 0/ is a symlink to the case the field lands in the real case. Copy 0/ whenever writeFields is requested.
recipe: buildOverlay(caseDir, region, {copyZero: Boolean(writeFields)})
after checkMesh read every requested field from the overlay and summarise {field, n, min, max, avg}
cross-check that max of nonOrthoAngle equals checkMesh maxNonOrtho
evidence: exp-025 tut-01_flange: writtenFields [{field: nonOrthoAngle, n: 19188, min: 0, max: 50.9531, avg: 15.668}] and maxNonOrtho 50.9531
before the fix the field appeared in `<case>/0/nonOrthoAngle` (real case), not in the overlay

cards.title: writeFlags is a top-level snappyHexMeshDict entry, not a debug sub-key
cards.when: writing layer fields (thickness, nSurfaceLayers) from snappyHexMesh
cards.statement: `writeFlags` sits at the top level of snappyHexMeshDict; placing it under `debug` fails with `FOAM FATAL IO ERROR: Attempt to return stream of primitives from a dictionary entry: debug`. The annotated dictionary shows the same placement.
recipe: write `writeFlags ( layerFields scalarLevels );` at the top level
keep `debug` for its own boolean switches only
verify in the log: `Writing fields with layer information:`
evidence: exp-025 tw02-gap-curvature: `FOAM FATAL IO ERROR … file: system/snappyHexMeshDict/debug at line 125 to 127` before the move
exp-025 tw02-gap-curvature after the move: 4 436 cells, maxNonOrtho 38.4975, PASS, 0/ has thickness/nSurfaceLayers

cards.title: gapMode/curvatureLevel/leakLevel/useLeakClosure/levelIncrement exist only in the .com line
cards.when: writing advanced snappy refinement on an OpenFOAM.org build
cards.statement: In the .org 14 sources there are zero occurrences of gapMode, curvatureLevel, leakLevel, useLeakClosure and levelIncrement, while the .com 2512/2606 dictionaries document them. Writing such a key on .org is a silent no-op, so the scaffolder must refuse or warn instead of emitting it.
recipe: check the target build through the capability matrix before writing an advanced key
com-only: gapMode, curvatureLevel, leakLevel, useLeakClosure, levelIncrement, locationsInMesh
on .org either drop the key with a warning or refuse with `switch to com2606`

cards.title: gapLevel exists in both lines; only gapMode is .com-only
cards.when: enabling gap refinement and choosing between the two OpenFOAM lines
cards.statement: The .org 14 sources carry gapLevel in refinementSurfaces and use it during refinement, so gapLevel itself is portable. The version matrix that marks gapLevel .com-only is wrong about the key; the real .com-only companion is gapMode.
recipe: on .org pass `gapLevel (numGapCells minLevel maxLevel)` per surface and omit gapMode
on .com add `gapMode` when the default mode is not what you want
keep the capability matrix as the source of truth, not a version table
evidence: exp-025 tw02-gap-curvature on com2606: `Big gap refinement iteration 0`, 4 436 cells, 38.4975°

cards.title: outsidePoints (leak detection) is supported by .org 14 as well
cards.when: deciding whether leak detection is available on an OpenFOAM.org build
cards.statement: refinementParameters reads `outsidePoints` in the .org 14 tree, so the key is not .com-only: it is supported but undocumented in the annotated dictionary. The capability matrix records it for both lines.
recipe: write `outsidePoints ((x y z) …)` with points in metres
expect the log line `Cell selection outsidePoints:`
do not gate the key on the distribution
evidence: plugins/mesh-build/data/capabilities.json — builds.org14.snappyKeys.outsidePoints = true, com2606 lists it in supportedButUndocumented

cards.title: Case discovery must descend into a case directory: sub-cases carry their own controlDict
cards.when: counting runnable tutorial cases or listing a family with sub-cases
cards.statement: A directory that already holds system/controlDict can still contain runnable sub-cases, each with its own controlDict (createPatch/TJunctionSwitching_createPatch/{bottom,inlet,top}). Stopping the walk at the first case undercounts the family; the per-family count is the sanity check.
recipe: walk up to four levels and keep descending after finding a controlDict
skip constant/system/0/ephemeral/postProcessing/Make, processor* and numeric time dirs
report counts per family as well as the total, so an undercount is visible
evidence: exp-025 list: com2606 51 cases / 51 controlDict (blockMesh 7, createPatch 5, snappyHexMesh 15, …), org14 9/9
PLAN-tutorial-2606 expected 47 cases — the four TJunction sub-cases were missed by the plan

cards.title: blockMesh/pipe cannot be expressed by a vertices+blocks+edges+faces spec
cards.when: round-tripping a blockMeshDict through a JSON spec
cards.statement: blockMesh/pipe uses named projected vertices, `projectCurve` edges and a `transform{}` block. A spec with plain vertices, edges and boundary cannot represent it, so the parser must refuse with a reason instead of silently distorting the geometry.
recipe: support `project (x y z) (names)` vertices, arc/spline/project edges, geometry{} and mergePatchPairs
refuse named vertices, projectCurve and transform{} explicitly
oracle check: cells/points/faces/maxNonOrtho must match the tutorial after regenerating the dict
evidence: exp-025 round-trip: 6 of 7 blockMesh cases identical (sphere 1 000/82.2028°, sphere7 4 600/51.0106°, spheroid7Projected 36 000/78.4345°, …), pipe refused

cards.title: A step that runs with cwd=<case> must not also receive a relative -case
cards.when: running mesh surgery utilities as engine.json steps
cards.statement: Engine steps execute with the case directory as cwd and also pass `-case {caseDir}`. With a relative caseDir the utility resolves the path twice and fails with `topoSet: cannot open root directory "…/case/experiments/…"`. Resolve the case directory once, before rendering the command.
recipe: makeContext must return `caseDir: resolve(caseDir)`
log the rendered command line in the step log so a doubled path is visible
run preflight against the same absolute path the step will use
evidence: exp-025 tut-13: before the fix `topoSet: cannot open root directory "…/tut-13…/experiments/exp-025_tutorial-2606/cases"`; after — topoSet exit 0 (182 ms), checkMesh exit 0 (179 ms)

cards.title: A bare `Mesh OK.` is not a quality pass: thresholds need checkMesh -meshQuality
cards.when: deciding whether a mesh is acceptable from a checkMesh log
cards.statement: Without -meshQuality, checkMesh only reports the numbers and fails on faces above 90°; it prints `Mesh OK.` for a mesh with 80.77° non-orthogonality. The same mesh under `checkMesh -meshQuality` says `Failed 1 mesh checks.`, so any gate must run with the threshold dictionary and judge the log text, not the exit code.
recipe: run `checkMesh -meshQuality` with an explicit meshQualityDict (overlay, so the case is untouched)
decide the verdict from the log text (`Mesh OK.` vs `Failed N mesh checks`) — checkMesh exits 0 in both cases
quote the violated metric and its threshold, not just the verdict
evidence: exp-025 tut-11_blockMesh_pipe, plain checkMesh: `Max aspect ratio = 11.1405 OK.`, `Mesh non-orthogonality Max: 80.7713 average: 27.091`, `Mesh OK.`, exit 0
same case through the gate: `Failed 1 mesh checks.` (nonOrthoFaces set written, 40 faces)
plugins/sim-core/lib/gate.js — verdict computed from log text via verdictOf(metrics)

cards.title: Feature extraction is surfaceFeatures on .org and surfaceFeatureExtract on .com — the dict name follows
cards.when: running the feature-extraction step of a snappyHexMesh pipeline
cards.statement: The utility and its dictionary are line-specific: .org ships `surfaceFeatures` with `system/surfaceFeaturesDict`, .com ships `surfaceFeatureExtract` with `system/surfaceFeatureExtractDict`. The same tutorial (flange) calls a different utility on each line, and the .org14 surfaceFeatureExtract exists only as a stub.
recipe: pick the utility from the capability matrix (featuresNew on .com, featuresOld on .org)
write the matching dictionary name — surfaceFeaturesDict vs surfaceFeatureExtractDict
on a .com build never rely on surfaceFeatureExtract-less pipelines: features refine explicit edges
evidence: exp-025 tut-01_flange (com2606): step surfaceFeatureExtract, 19 186 cells, 50.9531°, PASS

cards.title: Judge tutorial meshes with the `gate` profile, not the project profile
cards.when: running a shipped tutorial as an oracle rather than producing project geometry
cards.statement: The project profile (minVolRatio 0.05, maxBoundarySkewness 4) is tuned for our pore meshes and fails shipped tutorials on volume ratio alone: flange reports 48 faces below 0.05 while the `gate` profile passes it. A tutorial is an oracle for the step plan, so `gate` is the honest default; `project` stays available as a flag.
recipe: default profile for mesh_tutorial is `gate`
pass profile: "project" when the tutorial mesh itself must meet project thresholds
state the profile in the manifest (gate.profile) and in the experiment README
evidence: exp-025 tut-01_flange: gate PASS (19 186 cells, 50.9531°) vs project FAIL (48 faces volume ratio < 0.05)

cards.title: Two mesher passes in one tutorial: -s suffix keeps both logs, -writeAllFields records the mesh
cards.statement: `airfoilWithLayers` runs snappyHexMesh twice with different `fvSchemes geometry/type` and a `-s` suffix (`basic`, then `highAspectRatio`); `runApplication -s <x>` writes `log.<app>.<x>` instead of `log.<app>`, so the second pass never collides with the first. The following `checkMesh -s <x> -writeAllFields` numbers the pass and forces a write, otherwise nothing is written for a mesh-only run.
cards.when: A tutorial (or a user case) needs the same mesher run twice with edited dictionaries in one directory.
recipe: `foamDictionary system/fvSchemes -entry geometry/type -set basic` then `runApplication -s basic snappyHexMesh`
edit the dictionary again, then `runApplication -s highAspectRatio snappyHexMesh`
close each pass with `runApplication -s <same> checkMesh -writeAllFields` so the pass is numbered and the fields are written
improves: Tutorial runner: two-pass cases must not overwrite the first log
Mesh-only verdict for the second pass

cards.title: A collated parallel mesh stays on the ranks until redistributePar -reconstruct -constant
cards.statement: `sphere_gapClosure` keeps `fileHandler="-fileHandler collated"` in a variable, decomposes with `redistributePar -decompose -constant`, meshes with `mpirun snappyHexMesh -overwrite`, and only then calls `redistributePar -reconstruct -constant`. Without the reconstruct step the case has no whole mesh in `constant/polyMesh` — a gate or a renderer sees an empty case, not a mesh.
cards.when: A tutorial or case meshes in parallel with the collated file handler and must end with one mesh.
recipe: `runParallel -s decompose redistributePar -decompose -constant -fileHandler collated`
`runParallel snappyHexMesh -overwrite -fileHandler collated`
`runParallel -s reconstruct redistributePar -reconstruct -constant -fileHandler collated` before any gate or render
improves: Tutorial runner: collated cases end with a usable constant/polyMesh
Gate runs after reconstruct, not before
